title: Flexible Inputs with AsRef
goal: Accept any string-like type using the AsRef trait without forcing ownership.

sections.text: In languages like TypeScript or Python, a function accepting a string handles both string literals and heap strings automatically. In Rust, `&str` and `String` are distinct types, but `AsRef<str>` unifies them.

sections.caption: impl AsRef<str> accepts both &str and String.

sections.text: The `AsRef` trait provides cheap reference-to-reference conversion. When a function takes `impl AsRef<str>`, the caller can pass `&str`, `String`, or `&String` directly.
This avoids forcing callers to call `.as_str()` or `&` at every call site. The conversion happens via `msg.as_ref()` inside the function body.

sections.caption: Callers pass owned or borrowed strings without boilerplate.

sections.text: Generic conversion parameters add a small monomorphization cost to your binary. For private helper functions, `&str` remains the simpler choice.

explanation: Accept any string-like type using the AsRef trait without forcing ownership.
